territorial_scope.description: Extends to England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland and applies to relevant connectable products made available in the United Kingdom.

evidence.quote: extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland

summary.short: Sets security requirements for manufacturers of UK consumer connectable products, covering passwords, vulnerability reporting and minimum security update periods. It also sets deemed-compliance routes through ETSI EN 303 645, ISO/IEC 29147 and labelling schemes, excepted product categories, and statement-of-compliance content and retention rules, in force 29 April 2024 across the UK.
summary.long: Made under the Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022 and in force 29 April 2024 in England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland, these Regulations set security requirements for manufacturers of relevant connectable products. Schedule 1 requires unique or user-defined passwords, a published point of contact for security reports with acknowledgement and status updates, and a published defined support period for security updates. Regulation 5 applies these requirements to each manufacturer where there is more than one. Schedule 2 deems compliance where ETSI EN 303 645 or ISO/IEC 29147 provisions are met, or where a Japan JC-STAR STAR-1 or Singapore Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme label is held; Schedule 2A applies similar deemed compliance to statements of compliance. Schedule 3 lists excepted products, such as certain medical devices, computers, smart meters, electric vehicle charge points and vehicles. Schedule 4 sets statement-of-compliance content, and regulations 8 and 9 require manufacturers and importers to keep statements for the longer of ten years or the defined support period. Regulation 10 requires review at least every five years. This text itself contains no penalty provisions.

thresholds.measurement: Determined by the manufacturer's intended purpose, as defined in regulation 2(1) (the use for which the product is intended according to the data provided by the manufacturer)
thresholds.consequence: A computer listed in paragraph 5(1) of Schedule 3 that is designed exclusively for children under 14 is not an excepted product.
thresholds.conditions: Product is a desktop computer, laptop computer, or tablet computer without cellular network capability (Sch. 3 para. 5(1)); manufacturer's intended purpose is designed exclusively for children under 14.

evidence.quote: designed exclusively for children under 14 years old are not excepted products
“hardware” means a physical electronic information system, or parts thereof, capable of processing, storing or transmitting digital data;

“manufacturer’s intended purpose” means the use for which the product is intended according to the data provided by the manufacturer, including on the label, in the instructions for use, or in promotional or sales materials or statements;

“security update” means a software update that protects or enhances the security of a product, including a software update that addresses security issues which have been discovered by or reported to the manufacturer.
“defined support period” means the minimum length of time, expressed as a period of time with an end date, for which security updates will be provided;
“ETSI EN 303 645” means the European Standard on Cyber Security for Consumer Internet of Things: Baseline Requirements (ETSI EN 303 645 V2.1.1 (19th June 2020))
“ISO/IEC 29147” means the ISO/IEC 29147:2018 Information technology - Security techniques - Vulnerability disclosure standard (2nd edition, 2018)

“Japan JC-STAR STAR-1” means the Labeling Scheme based on Japan Cyber-Security Technical Assessment Requirements (JC-STAR) STAR-1 Conformance Requirements and Assessment Methods published by the Information-technology Promotion Agency, Japan
“Singapore Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme” means the Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme published by the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore
“factory default state” means the state of the product after factory reset or after final production or assembly;
“unique per product” means unique for each individual product of a given product class or type.

“good industry practice” means the exercise of that degree of skill, diligence, prudence and foresight which would reasonably and ordinarily be expected from a skilled and experienced cryptographer engaged in the same type of activity
“incremental counter” means a method of password generation in which multiple passwords are the same save for a small amount of characters which change per password to make them unique

“application programming interface key” means a string of characters used to identify and authenticate a particular user, product, or application so that it can access the application programming interface;
“cryptographic key” means data used to encrypt and decrypt data;

obligations.summary: Manufacturers of relevant connectable products must ensure passwords are unique per product or defined by the user, and that unique passwords are not incremental, public-derived, identifier-derived or otherwise guessable (Sch 1 para 1). Exclusions for cryptographic keys, certain pairing PINs and API keys are scope limits, not duties.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies to hardware and software of the product when not in factory default state, as set out in Sch 1 para 1(1)

obligations.summary: Manufacturers must publish at least one point of contact for reporting security issues, and the times at which the reporter will receive an acknowledgment and status updates. Information must be accessible, clear, transparent, given without prior request, in English, free of charge and without requesting personal information (Sch 1 para 2(2)-(3)).
obligations.conditional_on: Applies to hardware, pre-installed or installable software and software used for manufacturer's intended purposes, unless a smartphone or cellular tablet (Sch 1 para 2(1))

evidence.quote: The following information must be published—

obligations.summary: Manufacturers must publish the defined support period, and publish any new defined support period as soon as practicable when extended, in accessible, clear and transparent form in English, free of charge and understandable without technical knowledge. Where an invitation to purchase is published on the manufacturer's own or non-paid website, this information must be given equal prominence. The requirement is not met if the defined support period is shortened after publication (Sch 1 para 3(2)-(7)).
obligations.conditional_on: Applies to products capable of receiving security updates, as set out in Sch 1 para 3(1)

evidence.quote: The defined support period must be published.

obligations.summary: Where there is more than one manufacturer of a relevant connectable product, each manufacturer must meet any relevant Schedule 1 security requirement, or satisfy the deemed-compliance conditions in Schedule 2 for that requirement.

obligations.summary: The statement of compliance must include the product type and batch; the name and address of each manufacturer and any authorised representative; declarations that it is prepared by or for the manufacturer and of compliance with Schedule 1 or Schedule 2; the defined support period; the signatory's signature, name and function; and the place and date of issue. Where a standard is referenced, its identification number, version and date of issue must be included where applicable (Reg. 7; Sch. 4 para. 1-2).

enforcement.note: This instrument specifies security requirements, deemed-compliance conditions, excepted products and statement-of-compliance content. It contains no sanctions, fines, criminal penalties, revocation or blocking provisions. It is made under powers in the Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act 2022 (cited in the preamble and Explanatory Note as Part 1 of that Act), and the enforcement provisions, if any, are not stated in this text.
